column3: The Hebrew retains the image of the arm twice; BSB uses “strength.”
The Hebrew does not explicitly mark the dwelling as “My” and leaves the doer of good unnamed; BSB supplies “My” and describes good in Israel.
The Hebrew names the soul rather than the heart and contains no explicit word for “sword.”
The Hebrew names the soul where BSB uses “mind,” and speaks of “all the days.”
The Hebrew joins silver and a loaf of bread with “and”; BSB has “or.” The bread in the first clause is a round loaf.
